content.text:
So static HTML site works. I'll build a pure canvas-based pixel art game with no dependencies: index.html, style.css, game JS.

Design plan:

Title screen recreating the GoW3 Remastered menu in pixel art:
- Dark ash/storm background with swirling smoke, lightning, silhouette of Kratos on the right (pixel art portrait, 1/2 face lit), the Blades of Chaos blades in the foreground bottom center with fire glow, blood-splattered red banner for the title "GOD OF WAR" with "III" and "REMASTERED" under it, menu at left with items NEW GAME / LOAD / OPTIONS / TREASURES, red highlight on hover and white selected. Footer "X = SELECT" and "↑↓ MOVE". Add version text.
- Menu items functional: NEW GAME starts game; LOAD loads save (localStorage) if any; OPTIONS opens options submenu (sound volume, screen shake, pixel scale?); TREASURES shows unlocked extras.
- Keyboard + gamepad + touch (tap/click) + mobile.

Gameplay: a side-scrolling hack-and-slash "Clash of Olympus" pixel-art: Kratos sprite, enemies spawning, combos with Blades of Chaos (attack chain), dash, block? Health bar, rage meter, wave system, bosses. Playable and complete: 3 waves + boss (Zeus-ish / minotaur), win screen, death screen. Save progress (best wave / high score) to localStorage so LOAD works.

Art must be generated procedurally with canvas drawing code — pixel art drawn in code at low internal resolution (e.g., 480x270) and scaled with nearest-neighbor, plus a post-process scanline/vignette. Pixel art sprite drawing: I'll write a helper to draw sprites from string pixel maps with palettes. That gives authentic pixel art.

Let me plan technical details:

Canvas internal resolution 480x270 (16:9), scaled to fit. For mobile portrait, letterbox with black. Menu drawn on the low-res canvas.

I need a decent Kratos portrait pixel art at 480x270 — that's tough but I can draw him larger: portrait occupies right ~200x270. I can draw broad shapes: pale grey head with red tattoo stripe over left eye, beard, angry brow, scars; body silhouette dark with shoulder armor. Use layered ellipses/rects with pixel snapping. Doing hand-coded sprite maps might be more controllable. I'll write a "pixel art from string rows" utility with palette chars and build:

1. Kratos bust (large portrait) ~ 96x120 pixel art scaled 2x maybe. Hand-drawing 96x120 rows by hand is a lot of text but doable? That's ~11k chars. Hmm, that's heavy but yields good visuals. Alternative: procedural portrait with shapes — head oval, jaw, shading gradient, eye, brow, tattoo stripe, beard, crack scars. Procedural at 2x pixel grid could look decent.

I think a hybrid: procedural silhouette + shading for the big portrait (doesn't need to be exact), and hand-made sprite maps for Kratos gameplay sprite (24x32), enemies (16x24), etc.

Actually for the menu, the important thing is the vibe: dark stormy sky, ash particles, red title banner with blood drips, menu items, blades with glow, Kratos half-lit face on the right. Let's do procedural portrait carefully with dithering and lighting.

Let me design the menu composition for 480x270:
- Background: storm sky gradient (dark grey-blue at top, warmer near horizon), clouds via layered noise; distant jagged mountains; a churning smoke/ash texture; lightning flashes occasionally illuminating.
- Right: Kratos bust from x≈300 to 480, y from 40 to 270; face lit from left; scar; glowing eye? In reference his eye is dark with intensity. Blades crossing in the foreground bottom around x 180-330.
- Title: blood-red brush banner across x≈60..300, y≈28..70; "GOD OF WAR" in golden serif-ish pixel letters with dark outline; "III" in red beneath/behind; "REMASTERED" small gold letterspaced below.
- Menu: x≈62, y≈120..190; items NEW GAME, LOAD GAME, OPTIONS, TREASURES, CREDITS; selected item is bright white-red with a small red glyph marker, unselected muted dark red; hover with mouse.
- Bottom-left: "X  SELECT   ↑↓  NAVIGATE" prompt with a little controller button glyph; bottom-right "v1.0 · ASHES OF OLYMPUS".
- Subtle drifting embers.

Pixel font: draw text with a custom bitmap font (5x7) for UI, and a special "serif" title font - I can draw the title using a custom 8x12-ish bold font with per-letter offsets, plus outline, gold gradient and bevel. Simpler: use canvas font "Georgia" bold with pixelated rendering? Text drawn at low-res canvas then upscaled gets pixelated automatically, which can look fine but not truly pixel-art. For UI use bitmap font for crispness; for the title, draw using a wide custom uppercase font map with 7x9 glyphs scaled 2x and add shading. Let me create a 7x9 uppercase pixel font for the title and 5x7 for UI. Actually I can use one 5x7 font for UI and a separate title drawn with the same 5x7 scaled 3x with outline+gradient — but looks blocky. Let's craft a nice 7x9 font (chunky) for headings (NEW GAME menu at 2x) and title letters at 3x with gold gradient and dark red outline. GoW logo is serif with sharp serifs; pixelation approximation is acceptable.

Better: implement a proper bitmap font with mixed sizes: a 5x7 UI font and a 8x8 "bold" font used at 2x for menu with letterspacing. Title uses bold 8x8 at 3x with gradient fill per scanline + outline + blood splatter behind. Should look good.

Gameplay plan (side-scroller arena):
Internal res 480x270. Camera fixed with slight shake; ground at y=214. Parallax bg: stormy sky, temple columns, cliffs, ash particles, foreground rocks. Kratos at left area, moves left/right (A/D or arrows), jumps (W/Space), attacks (J/X or click), heavy attack (K), dash (Shift), special/blades throw (L) when rage full. Enemies: undead legionnaires (walk toward you, attack), harpies (fly, dive), minotaur boss at wave 5. Health bar top-left with portraits; rage meter; combo counter; wave banner; hit sparks, blood particles (pixel), screen shake; sound via WebAudio procedural (menu hum, hits, footsteps) — nice touch, with mute option.

Full game loop: Title → New Game → intro text ("ASHES OF OLYMPUS — WAVE 1") → 5 waves → boss → victory screen with stats → back to menu. Death → game over with Retry / Menu. Save best wave/score in localStorage; LOAD restores progress (start at highest wave reached? better: resumes at wave checkpoint with health). TREASURES shows unlocked relics (achievements) e.g. "Blades of Chaos", "First Blood (10 kills)", "Titan Slayer" etc. OPTIONS: master volume, screen shake, blood, CRT filter toggle; persisted.

Also pause menu with Esc/P.

Controls listed. Mobile touch controls: virtual joystick left, buttons right (attack, jump, dash, special). Ensure safe areas.

Implementation files:
- index.html (canvas + overlay text? all canvas) — use a single canvas and DOM only for a11y instructions. Keep everything canvas for pixel purity.
- style.css
- js/engine.js? Single game.js maybe 2000+ lines. Better split: src/font.js, src/art.js (sprites & portraits), src/audio.js, src/menu.js, src/game.js, src/main.js. Use ES modules (type=module) loaded from index.html; served statically. Modules work fine with file://? Not needed, we serve over http.

Let me structure:
- index.html
- styles.css
- src/main.js — boot, loop, input, scene management
- src/pixel.js — canvas helper, bitmap font, drawing utilities (pixel text, sprite from map, dither, noise)
- src/audio.js
- src/background.js — storm bg + Kratos portrait + blades drawing for menu
- src/menu.js — title/menu scene, options, treasures, credits, load
- src/game.js — gameplay
- src/save.js — localStorage progress
- src/touch.js maybe inside main.

Sprites: I'll hand-write pixel maps.

Kratos gameplay sprite: 16x24-ish, 3 frames idle + walk frames + attack frames. That's a lot of maps. Alternative approach: procedural character drawing with body parts (head, torso, arms, legs, blades) using rect/line primitives, and animate via angles. This gives smoother animation with less code and still pixel-ish when rendered at low res. I think procedural skeletal animation at low resolution looks pretty good and permits attack swings with flaming blades. But pixel-art authenticity favors sprite maps. Given time, procedural with hard-edged shapes + limited palette will look decent — plus flames/particles add flair.

Let me commit to a hand-drawn pixel sprite for Kratos at ~20x28 with a few frames, and enemies 14x20, boss 32x40. Hand-writing these maps: I can do rough but readable silhouettes with palette chars (skin, dark leather, gold, red tattoo, white ash). Let's allocate:

Kratos sprite 18x26, palette:
. transparent
K black/dark outline (#150f12)
S skin mid (#c9a184)
H skin light (#f0d7bd)
D skin shadow (#8d6a55)
R red tattoo (#b5252a)
r dark red (#6d1418)
G gold (#d9a63c)
g dark gold (#8a5f1c)
B leather brown (#4a3327)
b dark leather (#2a1c16)
A ash white (#ded6cc)
W blade steel (#cfd6dd)

Frames: idle (2 frames breathing), run (4 frames), jump, attack1, attack2, attack3? Attack animation could be done by rotating the blade separately (drawn procedurally as a glowing arc) while body sprite is a pose. Use body sprite poses (idle/run/jump/attack/hurt) and draw blades as rotating lines with glow. That's a good hybrid.

Actually simpler and reliable: build the character procedurally with layered rects in a pixel grid, with animations from key positions. Since canvas is low-res (480x270), Kratos is ~22x34 px. Procedural rects at integer coords give pixel look. I'll create a `drawKratos(ctx,x,y,facing,pose,t)` function drawing: legs, skirt, torso, shoulders, arms, head, beard, red tattoo stripe, blades with fire trails. This can be tuned and animated nicely.

Same for enemies: draw skeleton/undead soldier, harpy with wings, minotaur boss.

I'll go procedural for characters, bitmap for fonts, procedural for bg. It's more maintainable and animated.

Let me now think about the menu portrait in more detail, since it's the centerpiece the user asked for (recreate this menu in pixel art).

Portrait approach: draw at 480x270 canvas. Kratos head occupying right side, large (about 150x190 px), lit from the left with rim light from the sun. Procedural:

Head shape: define a polygon for skull+jaw. Using paths with fill and stepped shading? Canvas paths are antialiased, which breaks pixel art. I can draw on an offscreen low-res canvas (e.g., 480x270) — antialiasing still occurs on curves. To get crisp pixel art, disable smoothing doesn't affect path AA. Options: draw shapes then quantize colors? A trick: draw everything, then apply a paletted quantization + no smoothing when upscaling — AA pixels will get quantized to nearest palette color, creating jagged edges that look pixel-arty. That could work nicely: render portrait at 240x135 then upscale 2x into 480x270 buffer. Quantization: implement a simple palette snapping by nearest color (compute on ImageData). Might be slow per-frame; do it once (portrait is static except blinking/embers/sun flicker). Render portrait to offscreen once, quantize once, then blit with lightning overlay tint.

Yes: build portrait offscreen at 2x downres (240x135 region) and quantize to a 24-color palette. That gives chunky pixels. Similarly the blades could be part of that static portrait? Blades glow flickers — draw procedurally over it.

Let me design the portrait shapes:
- Big head tilted slightly, facing viewer-left. Coordinates in local space 0..200 x 0..270 mapped into right part.
- Skin palette: highlights cool grey-cream (#e8e0d4), mid (#b9ada1), shadow (#6d6259), deep shadow (#3a3330).
- Tattoo: red stripe from top-left of head down over left eye to cheek, dark red (#7d1b1b) with brighter (#c23a32) edge. Chain scar across right eye (X pattern) plus stitched scar (dark lines with small cross ticks).
- Beard: full short beard around jaw, dark grey with ash-white streaks.
- Eye: dark socket, white glint.
- Body: huge shoulders, ash-white skin with dark shading, leather straps, the golden gauntlet? Keep silhouette dark at bottom.

Rather than a strict likeness, evoke it.

Composition details also: red banner with blood: draw an organic splatter shape behind title area using random blobs & drips, dark red gradient, plus brighter red rim; title letters with gold gradient + shadow. Add "III" faint red behind.

Also ambient: drifting ash particles rising, lightning flash brightening clouds, distant thunder rumble audio on menu loop, thunder with screen flash.

Menu interaction: mouse hover selects item, click activates; keyboard up/down/enter; touch tap.

Transition: on NEW GAME press, a red/white flash and blood wipe to gameplay. Cool: draw expanding blood splatter mask over screen then reveal gameplay.

Gameplay details:

World: 480x270. Ground y=222. Kratos spawn x=120.
Player state: pos, vy, onGround, facing, hp 100, rage 0..100, combo timer, attack state machine with 3-hit chain, dash with i-frames, air attack.
Enemies types:
1. "LEGIONNAIRE" (undead): HP 30, walks, telegraphs attack, damage 8.
2. "HARPY": HP 20, flies sine, dives, damage 6.
3. "MINOTAUR" boss: HP 220, charges, ground slam shockwave, damage 15.
Waves: 1) 3 legionnaires; 2) 4 legionnaires + 2 harpies; 3) 5 legionnaires + 2 harpies; 4) 6 + 3; 5) BOSS + 2 harpies. Total waves 5. Between waves show "WAVE N" banner and heal a bit.

Combat feel:
- Attack: press J/X repeatedly for 3-hit chain; blades extend with fiery arcs; hit detection in front arc; knockback; hitstop 60ms; particles (blood red pixels, sparks gold); controller rumble? skip.
- Heavy: K slam causing shockwave when rage≥? Make heavy attack a spinning blades move requiring 25 rage? Keep simple: K = heavy slam (slower, more damage, small AoE), L = Rage of Sparta (costs full rage, screen-wide fiery burst, big damage).
- Jump attack.
- Dash (Shift) with brief invuln and afterimage.
- Enemies drop red orbs (XP) that fly to player and fill rage/score.
- Score, combo multiplier.
- Health pickups occasionally (green orb) maybe drop from boss.

HUD: top-left portrait + HP bar with gold frame; rage bar below; combo counter top-right big number; wave indicator; score. Boss health bar bottom center when boss active.

Death/Victory screens in pixel style with menu options.

Pause: overlay menu (RESUME, OPTIONS, MAIN MENU).

Save: localStorage key 'gow-pixel-save': {bestScore, maxWave, kills, unlocked:[...], settings:{volume, shake, blood, crt}}. LOAD from menu resumes at wave checkpoint (maxWave) with "continue" — if no save, disabled with "NO SAVE DATA". Actually "LOAD" should load saved run: store run progress when starting each wave: {wave, score, hp}. If none, show "NO SAVE DATA" message.

TREASURES: list of relics with locked/unlocked based on stats.

Audio: WebAudio: menu drone (two detuned saws + lowpass + noise), heartbeat? thunder noise bursts. Gameplay: hits (noise burst + low sine), sword swing (filtered noise sweep), jump, death, victory chord. Music? Procedural simple percussion/drone loop for battle. Keep modest but functional. Volume setting. Audio must start on user gesture.

CRT filter: optional scanlines + vignette; default on subtle. Toggle in options. Also pixel scale option maybe.

Accessibility: pause on blur, prevent scrolling on touch, safe area padding, responsive scaling.

## Objective
- Criar um menu pixel art inspirado em God of War III, com identidade visual baseada na referência e transformá-lo em um jogo completo e jogável.

## Requirements
- Construir uma tela de menu completa com estética pixel art.
- Incluir logo, retrato de Kratos, tempestade, lâminas de caos e elementos sangrentos.
- Criar combate de arena jogável, persistência, opções e controles sensíveis a teclado, toque e gamepad.
- Manter a experiência em português.

## Decisions
- Usar canvas 480×270 escalado para o viewport, com renderização intencionalmente pixelada.
- Construir toda a arte e o áudio procedurais, sem depender de assets externos.
- Usar localStorage para progresso e opções.
- Disponibilizar cinco ondas, incluindo inimigos e chefe Minotauro.

## Work State
### Completed
- Estrutura base do jogo em HTML/CSS/JavaScript.
- Tela de menu pixel art com cenário de tempestade, personagem, lâminas e logo.
- Navegação por menu, opções, tesouros e créditos.
- Motor de áudio procedural.
- Entrada por teclado, gamepad e controles móveis.
- Sistema de arena com ondas, inimigos, chefe, pontuação, combo e fúria.
- Persistência de progresso e opções.
- Telas de pausa, vitória e derrota.
- Renderização e testes visuais via navegador em diferentes estados.

### Active
- Nenhuma meta marcada como ativa; a implementação principal foi concluída.

### Blocked
- Nenhum bloqueio conhecido.

## Next Move
1. Validar o estado final em largura desktop e dispositivo móvel.
2. Revisar possíveis erros de jogo em todas as cinco ondas.
3. Ajustar o equilíbrio de dano, spawn e boss, caso necessário.
4. Fazer uma revisão final de menu, opções e persistência.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: estrutura principal da aplicação.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/styles.css`: layout, CRT, responsividade e controles de toque.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js`: inicialização, loop principal e troca de cenas.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/menu.js`: menu, opções, tesouros e créditos.

- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/battleArt.js`: personagens e fundo da arena.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/input.js`: teclado, toque e gamepad.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/save.js`: progresso e persistência.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/audio.js`: áudio procedural.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/pixel.js`: primitivas de desenho pixelado e tipografia.

## Objective
- Criar um jogo completo e jogável em pixel art inspirado em God of War III, com menu, combate de arena e experiência em português.

## Requirements
- Incluir menu pixel art com logo, retrato de Kratos, tempestade, lâminas do caos e elementos sangrentos.
- Oferecer combate com cinco ondas, inimigos e chefe Minotauro, além de opções, persistência e controles por teclado, toque e gamepad.
- Manter a experiência em português.

## Decisions
- Usar canvas 480×270 escalado para o viewport e arte e áudio procedurais.
- Persistir progresso e opções em `localStorage`.
- Traduzir também textos de combate, opções, tesouros e telas de pausa e fim de jogo.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implementação existente de menu, arte, áudio, controles, arena de cinco ondas, persistência e telas de estado.
- Iniciada a tradução dos textos do jogo e dos tesouros para português.
- Corrigida a lógica de pausa para consumir os eventos `pause` e `back` associados ao Escape.

### Active
- Validar as mudanças recentes no navegador, incluindo pausa, menu, opções, persistência e progressão pelas cinco ondas.

## Objective
- Criar e finalizar um jogo completo e jogável em pixel art inspirado no menu de God of War III, usando a imagem anexada como referência.

## Requirements
- Experiência em português, com menu pixel art, retrato de Kratos, tempestade, lâminas do caos e elementos sangrentos.
- Jogo de arena com cinco ondas, inimigos e chefe Minotauro; opções, progresso persistente e controles por teclado, toque e gamepad.
- Não fazer perguntas; assumir detalhes razoáveis.

## Decisions
- Canvas de 480×270 escalado ao viewport; arte e áudio gerados proceduralmente.
- Persistência de progresso e opções em `localStorage`.
- Textos de menu, combate, opções, tesouros e telas de pausa/fim traduzidos para português.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implementados menu, arte, áudio, opções, persistência, controles e arena de cinco ondas com telas de pausa, derrota e vitória.
- Corrigidos problemas descobertos em testes: `setupPointer is not a function`, import ausente de `ring`, captura de ponteiro em toques sintéticos e reforços que continuavam após derrotar o Minotauro.
- Testadas no navegador a pausa/retomada, navegação por toque, opções e créditos, persistência, progressão até a onda 5 e vitória; testados também controles de toque em tela móvel.
- Ajustados layout e textos para desktop e dispositivos móveis.

### Active
- Fazer uma validação final das últimas alterações e conferir o estado do repositório, pois as mudanças mais recentes ainda não tiveram verificação final documentada.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Rodar `node --check` em `src/*.js` e revisar `git status`.
2. Fazer uma verificação rápida no navegador após as últimas mudanças, incluindo menu, jogo, pausa e toque; corrigir qualquer erro restante.

## Relevant Files
- `src/game.js`: combate, ondas, HUD, pausa e estados de vitória/derrota.
- `src/menu.js`: menu, opções, tesouros, créditos e interação por toque.
- `src/input.js`: teclado, gamepad e controles de toque.
- `src/main.js`: inicialização, troca de cenas e responsividade.
- `src/save.js`: progresso, opções e tesouros persistidos.
- `src/battleArt.js`: arte da arena, inimigos e Minotauro.
- `src/titleArt.js`: identidade visual e arte do menu.
- `src/audio.js`: áudio procedural e ambiência.
- `index.html`: estrutura, ícone e instruções de controles.
- `styles.css`: layout responsivo e controles de toque.

## Important Context
- Alterações ainda não commitadas; não há informação de commit ou push.
- O servidor de desenvolvimento usado nos testes foi `http://localhost:3002`.
- Capturas de teste estão em `screenshots/`, diretório ignorado pelo Git.
